In machine learning: One choice of the model's settings (parameters, also called weights)
Loss: how wrong the model is with those settings
Settings that are all equally wrong
Derivative (one direction) or gradient (all directions at once)

On the orienteering course: How boldly you stride for a given slope
In machine learning: Learning rate (step size): step = learning rate * gradient
Overshooting: the learning rate is too high
Convergence: more steps no longer change the answer

On the orienteering course: A depression you can't see out of
Saddle, or a pass between hills
Judging the slope from a few footfalls, not a full survey
In machine learning: Stochastic or mini-batch gradient descent: the gradient is estimated from a sample of the data
